title: In need of fresh bullpen arms, Yankees claim John Schreiber off waivers from Royals: Source
content:
ANAHEIM, Calif. — A few days ago, New York Yankees manager Aaron Boone essentially admitted he was holding open tryouts in his bullpen because his reliever group has been overworked. Boone now has a new reliever in the mix.

The Yankees claimed John Schreiber off waivers from the Kansas City Royals, a team source confirmed to The Athletic. The source was granted anonymity because he wasn’t authorized to speak publicly about a transaction that hasn’t been made official yet. The New York Post first reported the waiver claim. The Yankees will owe Schreiber roughly $600,000 for the rest of the season. And by acquiring him ahead of Sept. 1, he will be postseason eligible for the Yankees.

Schreiber has had a rocky season with the last-place Royals. He has a 45.4 percent ground-ball rate, one of the highest marks of his career, but his 18 percent strikeout rate and 11 percent walk rate are less-than-encouraging metrics. He has a 4.87 FIP, even though his ERA is a more respectable 3.65. Part of the reason why Schreiber’s ERA looks good on the surface is that he has benefited from a low .248 batting average in balls in play, despite poor metrics.

The Yankees have had success with late-season bullpen adds in the past. Last year, the Yankees signed Paul Blackburn after the New York Mets parted ways with the right-hander. Blackburn has turned into one of MLB’s best relievers this year. Tim Hill and Luke Weaver were also late-season pickups for the Yankees who turned out to be exceptional pitchers out of the bullpen.

None of those pitchers had sparkling numbers before joining the Yankees. Maybe Schreiber can be the latest success story for the Yankees’ pitching department.
